definition: When a model is too simple or undertrained to capture the underlying patterns in the data.
details: Underfitting produces poor performance on both training and validation data, and is typically addressed by increasing model capacity, training longer, or improving feature representations.

explainer.lead: Underfitting is when a model is too simple or undertrained to capture the patterns in the data. It matters because it yields poor performance on both training and validation data.

tiers.eli5: It's like trying to draw a detailed picture with a single thick crayon, so the result misses the fine detail entirely.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers address underfitting by increasing model capacity, training longer, or improving feature representations. A pitfall is mistaking it for overfitting when training performance itself is already poor.
tiers.paperLevel: Underfitting produces poor performance on both training and validation data; remedies include increasing model capacity, training longer, and improving feature representations.

explainer.example: A linear model trained on clearly nonlinear data performs badly on both the training and validation sets, showing underfitting.
